source.title: Towards Principled Evaluations of Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability and Control
source.authors: Aleksandar Makelov; Georg Lange; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study uses the GPT-2 Small IOI circuit and its cross-sections as a setting for evaluating supervised feature dictionaries and SAEs. It does not test whether the selected attention heads form a faithful, complete, or minimal circuit.
record.gate_note: The study reports IOI behavior under SAE reconstruction and feature-editing interventions. These results concern the performance of its feature dictionaries, not direct ablations of the proposed circuit or a test of whether components outside it change IOI performance. The paper also discusses feature interpretations consistent with head roles, but these are not tests of the circuit-selection claim.
record.test_reason: The study takes the Wang et al. IOI circuit (its 26 heads and cross-sections) as given. It uses it as a testbed for evaluating supervised feature dictionaries and SAEs. It never ablates or patches the circuit to test faithfulness, completeness or minimality, backup heads, other models, other circuit-finding methods, or prompt variants. Its circuit-relevant side observations are qualitative: SAE features are consistent with head roles, and supervised feature interactions in name-mover attention match the circuit description. One new detail is that L10H0 also inhibits IO. These observations are interpretations conditional on the circuit, not tests of it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors propose supervised feature dictionaries as a benchmark for SAEs on IOI in GPT-2 Small. They find SAEs learn interpretable IOI features but control the model less well than supervised features, with task SAEs better than full-distribution SAEs. They also report feature occlusion and over-splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The original work identifies and evaluates a head-level IOI circuit. This paper instead uses supervised dictionaries and SAEs to reconstruct and edit activations at selected IOI circuit locations, evaluating feature dictionaries rather than rediscovering or validating the circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SAE control differs by dictionary training distribution: task-specific SAEs achieve more control with fewer edited features than full-distribution SAEs. The paper also notes that S-edit results can be hard to resolve because no intervention is already close to the supervised edit.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 Small on the study's 3-template IOI distribution: about 91% accuracy, logit difference about 3.3, correct-name logit higher in about 99% of examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 Small performs IOI well on a narrower template distribution with unseen test templates.

fits_no_version.finding: At IOI circuit cross-sections, supervised mean dictionaries reconstruct and edit attributes well (>80% agreement with ground-truth edits). Task SAEs are weaker, and full-distribution SAEs and frozen-decoder SAEs are weaker still.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The quality of feature-dictionary reconstruction and sparse control at IOI circuit locations depends on dictionary type.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-level attention decomposition shows the L10H0 name mover inhibits both S and IO tokens, unlike L9H6 and L9H9. The authors state SAE features are consistent with Wang et al. head roles for all heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Head roles in the IOI circuit are reflected in, and refined by, feature-level decompositions of head activations.

record.problems: The authors limit the study to one task and one language model and state that SAE hyperparameter tuning was not exhaustive. Some S-edit comparisons are described as within the margin of error, without a quantified uncertainty measure in the text. Several detailed results appear in figures rather than as text values.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-cross-section and per-edit values in Figures 2–4 and Appendix Figures 22–31 are not transcribed separately; the paper's aggregate textual descriptions are recorded. Feature-interpretation counts and qualitative analyses are omitted because they report SAE interpretation results rather than tests of the claimed circuit.

untested.parts: Faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the 26-head circuit are not tested. Head-class roles are only checked qualitatively, via feature content and feature-level attention decompositions (App. A.7, A.13).
No ablation of name movers and no measurement of backup takeover. Backup behaviour is only mentioned descriptively (App. A.1).
Only GPT-2 Small and only the IOI task.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods. Ablation choices are made for feature dictionaries, not for circuit evaluation.
Circuit faithfulness under different ablations, metrics or distributions is not evaluated.
Uses ABB/BAB orders and a held-out template, but does not compare circuit components across variants. Shifted templates are only asserted to give the same dictionary results.

missing.what: Qualitative feature-level evidence on head-class roles: S/Pos/IO interactions in name-mover QK, L10H0 IO inhibition, and direct effects from S-I heads and layer-9 name movers onto L10H0 queries. This is not a test of V1, but researchers comparing studies may want it.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test call holds. All rows correctly carry versions ["none"]. Their states describe dictionary performance rather than any claim version, which is acceptable since they are unlinked. No verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not independently test the 26-head, 7-class circuit, its faithfulness, completeness or minimality, or whether the circuit's head classes have their stated roles under circuit-level patching.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads and test whether backup heads take over.
Uses GPT-2 Small only; does not test the circuit in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, circuit ablation types, or circuit-evaluation metrics.
Compares feature-dictionary reconstruction and editing results, not the circuit's faithfulness or completeness under different circuit ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions.
Uses IOI prompts with ABB/BAB orders and held-out templates for its task, but does not test whether the same circuit components carry IOI across those variants.

relation.reason: Selects circuit locations and expected attribute roles from Wang et al.; reports feature-dictionary reconstruction, control and interpretability performance.

tranche.reason: Uses the established IOI circuit as a testbed for supervised dictionaries and SAE evaluations; does not evaluate the head circuit's faithfulness, completeness or minimality.

source_check.notes: R4–R11 accurately describe method benchmarks, but the row-scope rule flags own-method comparisons: retain these as contextual results, not phenomenon-evidence rows. Their states describe dictionary performance; no claim version is tested.
